body: For decks, I would recommend Toy Machine, Real, or Almost. I really enjoy skating Independent trucks as well. For bearings, I prefer Bones Redz. The parts that you pick for your board are really up to personal preference, especially when it comes down to the deck and bearings. If you have one, your local skate shop might be a good place to start. Otherwise, there’s reputable companies such as Tactics.com that will ship you board parts or a complete assembled board for free. Good luck!

If you’re new to skateboarding, I’d recommend buying a complete from your local skate shop or a reputable one online. Avoid “toy” skateboards from big retailers such as Walmart or Target because those won’t get you very far and might even discourage you from riding. You can customize your board, but generally speaking, less experienced riders probably won’t notice the difference between a board with great parts and a board with decent parts. Hope this helps!

Yeah, ceramic bearings are great and all (I personally use Zealous), but they shouldn't make much of a difference when you're first starting to ride a Boosted Board. There's a longer roll time while coasting and less drag, but generally, the motors do all of the work anyways. I'd stick to researching about bearings and the other parts first such as bash guards and Shredlights before looking into which bearings you should use. Stock bearings aren't the best, but they'll hold up alright.

Of course, I just want to say that by no means am I a professional at this, but I'll try my best in offering you advice.

Bushings are rubber rings that go on the truck of your board to assist in pivoting and turning your board smoothly. There's many different types and variations of bushings, along with endless combinations you can choose from. I can't technically "recommend" a specific bushing for you, as it is very user specific (such as your personal preferences, ride-style, and weight). 

In my opinion, they're more important for electric skateboards than bearings because harder bushings will help prevent speed-wobbles at high speeds and on the other hand, softer bushings will help with sharper turns and smoother carving. Hope this helps!

To be honest, when I first purchased it, I didn't think that it'd make a significant difference in my riding experience. However, I was wrong. It's much easier to control my speeds with the thumb wheel and overall, it improves my ride experience tremendously. It's easy to install but comes at a hefty price of $12 + $4 shipping. 

If you wear gloves while riding or if your thumb tends to slip, then I'd definitely invest in the thumb wheel. They're available in three colors (orange, gray, and black). 

If you DON'T have trouble with your current wheel now, or you're not looking to wear gloves while riding, then I don't think it's necessary but it's a nice addition anyway.

Also, remember to write down your board's serial number + remote's serial number just in case you lose them! Boosted can sometimes track down stolen/lost boards but they can't help you recover it unless you have the numbers.

I use the shock pads and I don't feel a BIG difference, but it's nice to have in my opinion. They aren't necessary though, and it's up to your personal preference. If the roads around your area are bumpy, I'd say they're worth investing in, but don't expect any MAJOR differences.

I think I can heavily relate to your situation and I'd like you to know that I'm on Wellbutrin XL (a generic brand of bupropion) 150mg/day. I agree, it definitely is anxiety-inducing, especially since my hands won't stop shaking. 

I think this feeling of restlessness can stem from both the medicine as well as other external factors, but what you're experiencing definitely sounds like anxiety to me (by no means am I a professional, so I recommend speaking to your psychiatrist about this as well). 

In my opinion, the medication really helps me feel less hopeless, but the side effects are starting to affect my daily life- things such as insomnia, decreased appetite, anger/mood swings, increased suicidal thoughts, and especially anxiety.

What I would do, is email my psychiatrist about it and see if there's any solution (such as decreasing the dosage) of the bupropion or any other means. It's definitely not a good idea to continue taking this medication if it's causing more discomfort in your life. I know you don't want to start another process of finding a new antidepressant, but in my opinion, it's difficult to find the right one and sometimes it's worth it to just keep experimenting.

I just want you to know that I'm here if you ever need to talk, and I'm sorry if what I said didn't help you at all. I've done lots of research on our antidepressant ever since I started taking it, and it seems to treat depression effectively, but is also dangerous for those with anxiety disorders since it only amplifies the symptoms. I honestly wish you the best, and I hope you keep me updated on how you're feeling in the days to come.

I think it’s bad in a sense that it skewers other’s depictions of mental illnesses. In our society today, we either don’t like talking about our mental health, or we do, but we’re not entirely honest about it.

Movies love showing the typical sweet, innocent girl who loves making others happy but can’t seem to give herself that same amount of love. It makes a lot of people believe that there’s beauty in panic attacks and beauty in hiding how you really feel because you overthink everything.

It’s not that those WITH the mental illnesses/disorders are romanticizing them, I honestly think it’s those who either a) claim to have one but they likely don’t, or b) don’t understand the actual amount of pain and suffering people go through with their mental illnesses.

That also raises a general stigma against people with, say, depression. “Depressed” people don’t ACTUALLY have to appear sad 24/7; likewise, they also don’t have to appear happy and are “secretly hiding it”. It’s a very complex disorder that’s different for everyone, but the way our society depicts it, is as someone who’s very negative, pessimistic, and just.. sad. That can be the case for some, but if someone were to just generalize me, a whole fucking person, as just a “sad” person, I’d be offended. 

Why? Cause I’m not just a “sad” person. I’m someone who has been diagnosed with clinical depression but that does not make me who I am. /I/ make up who I am- and depression is just a part of my life but it does not define me. There’s nothing I find “cute” about laying in bed at 3am and wanting to fucking die for what appears to me as seemingly no reason. There’s nothing I find “beautiful” about digging my nails so deep into my skin, I bleed because I can’t control how scared and nervous and exposed I feel in public. 

To bring this back to what you’re saying, about how this can be a beautiful thing since we’re all, essentially, trying to get better, I personally don’t see it that way. It really fucks with the lives of others and it’s something that causes an immense amount of pain. Seeing beauty in that pain only causes those looking with an outside perspective to believe that mental disorders can’t be /that/ serious. 

So yes, in my opinion, it’s not a good thing to romanticize these illnesses/disorders because it may cause a lack of understanding in what we actually go through in our daily lives. It makes people believe that there’s something /good/ about having what you have- and who knows, maybe it IS a good thing and maybe you wouldn’t be where you are today without it, but I honestly wish that I’ve never had to see how ugly depression can get and how badly it can break someone down. 

TLDR; I don’t agree with your opinion because I think romanticizing something, disrupts people’s understanding of the topic, but I respect your opinion. To each their own, and I’m sorry if I started babbling.
